chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Fever for a night is an expiation for what is before it and what is after it.

key_terms.لِمَا بَعْدَهَا: For what is after it (future sins)
key_terms.لِمَا قَبْلَهَا: For what is before it (past sins)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of fever in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that a single night of fever serves as a comprehensive expiation (kaffarah) for a believer's sins, covering both past and future transgressions. This teaching underscores the Shia understanding of illness not merely as a trial, but as an active mechanism of divine mercy and spiritual purification, where physical suffering is transformed into a means of erasing minor sins and elevating one's rank in the hereafter.
